summary: Venturis Financial — request-replay causing stuttered streaming and sudden rate spike
description:
Issue summary:
Venturis reported intermittent long-tail stutter in streaming completions followed by a sudden token-usage spike and invoice alert. Customers observed repeated short pauses mid-stream and occasional duplicate partial sentences. Impact: degraded UX for real-time flows and unexpected billing increase for the customer.

Impact:
- ~7% of Venturis production streams in eu-west experienced mid-stream stutters or repeated fragments between 09:12–11:40 UTC on 2026-03-10.
- Token accounting showed a ~2.4x spike on affected connections during the window, triggering an invoice alert.
- Client-facing symptoms: partial duplicate phrases in audio/video captioning pipeline (real-time chat).

Timeline (high level):
- 09:10 UTC: Venturis support pinged #support with report of intermittent stutter and billing alert.
- 09:18 UTC: Support created SUP-199204 and escalated to SRE/Infra.
- 09:25–09:50 UTC: Triage, mitigation (temporarily increased connection timeouts), and early hypothesis logged.
- 10:05 UTC: Identified elevated router retry rate from Private Gateway LB for Venturis VPC.
- 10:40 UTC: Traffic-shedding rule applied for suspected replay flows; stutter rate dropped.
- 11:20 UTC: Deployed router dedupe patch and SDK idempotency header in canary; confirmed on Venturis traffic.
- 12:30 UTC: Billing team ingested corrected token counts and issued preliminary credit.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate Venturis streaming workload with short messages and frequent re-connections.
2) Configure Private Gateway LB to mark backend as unhealthy for 1 retry on transient 502s.
3) Trigger a transient backend restart; observe client SDK retries without idempotency header causing router to re-emit partially-buffered request segments.

Observed logs & dashboards:
- router-retry-metrics (eu-west-1): spike from baseline 0.3% -> 9.8% during 09:12–10:05 UTC.
- Prod-Streaming-Connections: increased session restarts and duplicated partial-kv writes in router logs.
- Billing-pipeline: token ingestion showed duplicate token batches with identical request IDs but different connection IDs.
- sample router log excerpt: "2026-03-10T09:24:17Z WARN router: replayed request id=abcd1234 conn=conn-78 -> emitted 2 event batches"

Initial mitigation taken:
- Applied traffic-shed rule at Private Gateway to route Venturis traffic to a conservative path with dropout suppression to stop cross-connection replays.
- Increased client-connection idle timeout and temporarily disabled aggressive LB retries in the customer’s VPC control plane.
- Coordinated with Venturis to deploy SDK patch that sets X-Idempotency-Key per logical request.

Customer impact statement for Venturis support: 
We temporarily shifted your traffic to a conservative routing profile to stop repeated replays and issued a provisional credit for the affected window. We verified restored streaming fidelity after dedupe and SDK updates.
comments: 2026-03-10T09:22:11Z - Support (Elena Morales): Received initial report from Venturis via email. Noted "stutters" and spike in token usage. Escalating to infra.
2026-03-10T09:30:04Z - SRE (Marcus Nguyen): Investigating router retry metrics (eu-west). Early sign: Private Gateway LB returning transient 502s leading to rapid client retries.
2026-03-10T10:12:45Z - Infra (Liam O'Connor): Applied traffic-shedding rule for Venturis VPC. Observed immediate drop in stream-stutter alerts on dashboard.
2026-03-10T11:05:02Z - SDK (Priya Shah): Deployed canary SDK v1.4.3 with X-Idempotency-Key header; canary traffic showed no duplicates on router logs.
2026-03-10T11:48:29Z - Billing (Rita Gomez): Reprocessed token batches for 09:00–12:00 window; detected duplicate batch ids. Issued provisional credit and flagged for invoice adjustment.

2026-03-12T09:00:00Z - Customer (Venturis Support, James Li): Confirmed that streaming behavior returned to normal and thanked the team for rapid response. Asked for post-incident writeup and permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: LB transient health-check behavior caused backend connection resets; combined with non-idempotent client retries produced repeated partial request frames.
Hypothesis 2: Router lacked connection-level dedupe for multi-segment streaming packets; duplicate partial frames were being forwarded as new token events to the billing pipeline.
Logs show identical request IDs reprocessed across distinct connection IDs which indicates replay, not independent requests.
Kernel of the issue isolated to private gateway LB config (aggressive retry on 502) + SDK behavior (immediate retry without idempotency key).
Reproduction achieved in staging by forcing a 1s backend drain and observing duplicate partial frames emitted when SDK retries were enabled.

Root cause: combination of (a) LB retries marking backend unhealthy causing mid-stream reconnects, (b) client SDK retrying the in-flight request without idempotency, and (c) router forwarding logic that treated partial frames as new message units for token accounting.
Impact to billing: duplicate frames were double-counted because token ingestion keyed on requestID+connectionID; when connectionID changed but requestID unchanged, duplicate batch ingestion occurred.
Risk assessment: Medium-high for private customers with aggressive LB configs and real-time streaming workloads. Not present in hosted API where router dedupe and stricter LB configs exist.
resolution_summary: Fixed by three coordinated changes: (1) patched router to perform cross-connection deduplication for recent request IDs (PR 3456), (2) updated SDK to set a per-request X-Idempotency-Key and backoff behavior (SDK PR 1209), and (3) rolled back aggressive retry policy in Private Gateway LB templates. After changes verified on Venturis traffic, stutter and duplicate tokens returned to baseline. Billing reprocessing removed duplicate batches and a credit was applied to Venturis' account.
rollback_notes: No rollback required; fixes were additive. Canary for router dedupe was rolled back briefly for additional logging, then re-applied. All changes validated in canary (Venturis tag) before full rollout.
post_incident_actions: Create a permanent Private Gateway LB profile that disables immediate retry-on-502 for streaming routes (owner: Infra, due 2026-03-20).
Add router-level token-ingestion dedupe check keyed by requestID only (owner: Billing/Router, due 2026-03-18).
Ship SDK v1.4.5 with idempotency header and client backoff by default (owner: SDK, due 2026-03-16).
Add automated alert in Prod-Streaming-Connections for sudden requestID replays >1% (owner: Observability, due 2026-03-17).
Follow up with Venturis for final billing reconciliation and confirm credit applied (owner: Customer Success, due 2026-03-13).
